Let each large square have side length \(2\), so its total area is \(4\). Its four quadrants each have area \(1\).

- **A:** The black region is one whole quadrant, so its area is \(1\).
- **B:** Each of the two black triangles is half a quadrant, so the total is
  \[
  2\left(\frac12\right)=1.
  \]
- **C:** Each black diamond has perpendicular diagonals of length \(1\), so each has area
  \[
  \frac{1\cdot1}{2}=\frac12.
  \]
  Thus the two diamonds have total area \(1\).
- **D:** Each of the four black triangles has base \(1\) and height \(\frac12\), hence area \(\frac14\). Their total area is
  \[
  4\left(\frac14\right)=1.
  \]

All four squares therefore contain the same total black area.
